data.description:
## Context / Problem

Epic `inferior-seaborgium-aruanas` makes release a first-class rebar ticket field synced both ways with Jira's `fixVersions`. Its approach step 1 requires an ADR before any code, so the later children (reducer, inbound, outbound, missing-version alert, surfaces) build against one recorded design instead of re-deciding it. The operator settled the core decisions on 2026-11-05 (epic description and comments). This ADR records those and settles the points the epic delegates to the ADR: the replayed event carrier, the field name, the `FIELD_CONTRACT` class, name identity and renames, and archived/deleted versions.

## Approach

Write `docs/adr/0123-jira-fix-versions-release-field.md` (next free number: the last marker is `docs/adr/.numbers/0122`, and no open Gerrit change claims 0123 as of 2026-11-09) with a `## Decision` section of numbered items:

1. **Field shape.** Compiled ticket state gains `releases`: a list of Jira version names (strings), default `[]`, insertion-ordered, no duplicates. Names only; no release records, no release status or dates (operator decision 2026-11-05).
2. **Event carrier.** A new event type `RELEASE_DELTA` with body `{"added": [...], "removed": [...], "source"?: "inbound"}`, folded by a new `process_release_delta` with exactly the semantics of `process_tag_delta` (`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:429-449`): removals first, then additions, so an add beats a remove in one event. Rejected alternative: generalizing `TAG_DELTA` with a field selector. An older clone that knows `TAG_DELTA` but not the selector would fold release names into `tags`, which is silent corruption; a new event type instead takes the preserve-and-ignore path for unknown types (`src/rebar/reducer/_version.py:8-16`). `SCHEMA_VERSION` goes from 5 to 6 because a new event body type is added, as v3 did for `TAG_DELTA` (`docs/event-schema.md` section "Schema version & forward compatibility"). Rollout is readers before writers: upgrade the reconcile host first, as that section already prescribes.
3. **Symmetry class.** `FIELD_CONTRACT["releases"]` is `ADD_WINS` with conflict class `set` and `outbound_name="fixVersions"`, mirroring `labels` (`src/rebar/reconciler/_field_contract.py:108-119`). `conflict_resolver.FIELD_CLASSES` gains `"releases": "set"`.
4. **Inbound.** Set-diff Jira `fixVersions[].name` against local `releases`, as `_diff_labels_inbound` does (`src/rebar/reconciler/inbound_collection_diffs.py:194-214`). Write `RELEASE_DELTA` with `source="inbound"`, reading current state only to suppress no-ops and skipping the write when the reducer fails, as `_inbound_update_apply_labels` does (`src/rebar/reconciler/apply_inbound_events.py:322-389`).
5. **Outbound.** ADD names that are local and not on the Jira issue; REMOVE only names in the local ever-seen intent set (non-inbound `RELEASE_DELTA` additions plus `SNAPSHOT` releases), as `_diff_labels` does with `local_label_intent` (`src/rebar/reconciler/outbound_labels.py:43-85`). Jira writes use per-item update verbs only, never a whole-list set: Cloud `PUT /rest/api/3/issue/{key}` with `{"update":{"fixVersions":[{"add":{"name":N}}]}}` (or `remove`); Data Center `issue.update(update={"fixVersions":[...]})`, the same verb the DC label remove uses (`src/rebar/reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/_issues.py:196`).
6. **Same-pass conflicts.** Outbound wins, through the existing outbound-context suppression (`src/rebar/reconciler/inbound_differ.py:298-322`), extended from labels to releases.
7. **Identity and renames.** A release is identified by its name; Jira version names are unique per project (Jira Cloud OpenAPI `Version.name`: "The unique name of the version"). A rename of a version that reached rebar from Jira surfaces as remove old plus add new on the bound tickets. A name set from rebar that later stops existing in the project follows item 8.
8. **Missing version.** The bridge reads each bound project's version list once per pass (Cloud `GET /rest/api/3/project/{key}/versions`; DC `project_versions`). It does not write an outbound ADD for a name the project lacks, keeps the name on the rebar ticket, writes one `BRIDGE_ALERT` per (ticket, name) with reason `release-version-missing:<name>`, retries every pass, and writes a resolving `BRIDGE_ALERT` once the name is written or is no longer on the ticket. A withheld name still counts as an outbound ADD for item 6, so the inbound set-diff cannot strip it. The bridge never creates Jira versions (operator decision 2026-11-05).
9. **Archived and deleted versions.** An archived version is treated like a missing one for outbound ADD (withheld, alert reason `release-version-archived:<name>`), because Jira's issue editor does not offer archived versions and the API outcome is unverified. An archived name already on a Jira issue still syncs inbound, and an outbound REMOVE of it is attempted normally. Released versions are written normally. A deleted version is absent from the project list, so item 8 applies; when Jira strips a deleted version from its issues, the inbound diff removes it locally.
10. **Out of scope.** Jira "Affects versions" (`versions`) is not synced. There is no inheritance through the parent hierarchy: `list --release X` returns exactly the tickets whose own `releases` contain X. No config key: the field syncs whenever the bridge runs.
11. **Surfaces.** `rebar edit --add-release/--remove-release/--set-releases` (the `--set-releases` delta is computed against observed releases, add-wins, like `--set-tags`), `rebar list --release`, `rebar show` output, the library `edit_ticket` keywords `add_releases`/`remove_releases`/`set_releases`, and the MCP edit/list parameters plus the read `outputSchema`s.

Add an `## Evidence` section recording the read-only Jira checks of 2026-11-09 (PST) against the production site:
- `GET /rest/api/3/field`: `fixVersions` schema `{"type":"array","items":"version","system":"fixVersions"}`.
- `GET /rest/api/3/issue/REB-7015/editmeta`: no `fixVersions` entry (labels lists operations `add`, `set`, `remove`).
- `GET /rest/api/3/project/{key}/versions` on all 144 projects: 0 versions in each; a JQL search for `fixVersion is not EMPTY` returns 0 issues. So no project on the site can exercise a per-item add/remove without creating a version, which this epic must not do in production.
- Atlassian's "Updating an Issue via the JIRA REST APIs" page lists Fix Versions as supporting Set, Add and Remove by version id or name.
- The Jira Cloud OpenAPI description of `PUT /rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}` says the endpoint "doesn't check screen configurations to determine if a field is editable". That contradicts the epic's prerequisite that Fix versions must be added to REB's edit screen before rebar can write it. The production-verification child resolves it live; until then the screen change stays listed as a prerequisite.

Then add the ADR to the "Reconciler" list in `docs/adr/README.md` after the 0121 entry, and create the marker `docs/adr/.numbers/0123` holding the ADR filename.

## Scope

- `docs/adr/0123-jira-fix-versions-release-field.md` (new)
- `docs/adr/.numbers/0123` (new marker)
- `docs/adr/README.md` (index entry)

No code or tests change. This is documentation only, so there is no new testable behavior; the ADR-number gate and the docs tests in `make verify` are the checks.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/adr/0123-jira-fix-versions-release-field.md` exists with `**Status:** Accepted` and a `## Decision` section whose numbered items cover all 11 points in the Approach: field shape; the `RELEASE_DELTA` carrier with the rejected `TAG_DELTA` generalization and its reason; `SCHEMA_VERSION` 6 with readers-before-writers rollout; the `FIELD_CONTRACT`/`FIELD_CLASSES` classes; inbound; outbound with intent-gated REMOVE and per-item verbs; same-pass suppression; name identity and renames; missing-version alerting with the bridge-never-creates rule; archived and deleted versions; out-of-scope items (Affects versions, inheritance, config key); surfaces.
- [ ] The ADR's `## Evidence` section records the 5 read-only findings above with the endpoint used for each, and names the screen-check contradiction.
- [ ] `docs/adr/.numbers/0123` exists and `python scripts/check_adr_numbers.py` exits 0.
- [ ] `docs/adr/README.md` links `0123-jira-fix-versions-release-field.md` in the Reconciler list.
- [ ] `env -u JIRA_URL -u JIRA_USER -u JIRA_API_TOKEN make verify` exits 0 on the commit pushed for review.
data.title: Record the release-field design for Jira fix versions in ADR 0123
